fallos_mitigaciones: 'Forgetting' phenomena from over-compression: quantified failure breakdown shows ~15% of LOCOMO failures are retrieval errors and ~5% are information loss from compression (S3.1); mitigated via dual-granularity storage (Level-1 summary + Level-2 raw text) with dynamic escalation to raw Level-2 text only when the lightweight module detects 'contextual incompleteness' (a 'forgetting' state), plus a reflection module that iteratively refines/decomposes queries when answers are incomplete (S3.2-3.4).
cita: Wang et al. (2026). HyMem: Hybrid Memory Architecture with Dynamic Retrieval Scheduling.
notes: S3.1: dual-granularity storage -- Level-1 event summaries (vectorized E(si)=ei) + Level-2 raw dialogue text (pi), with explicit many-to-one links from Level-1 to Level-2 'to support memory backtracking during the recall stage' -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(event units)+SEMANTICA(distilled summaries: context/time/location/participants), representacion=HIBRIDA, operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION, and the explicit backtracking link IS a provenance/verification path from compressed to raw source -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F. S4.5 Fig.6: LLMLingua-2 compression-ratio sweep shows accuracy degrades as compression increases; event-level compression (~30% of original length) beats LLMLingua-2 at matched ratios, confirming aggressive/naive compression hurts -> NEGATIVO(b). benchmarks: NINGUNO (no standardized external benchmark evaluated; explicit scope limitation -- LOCOMO deferred to future work, S5.1/S6.3); internal Criterion.rs micro/macro-benchmarks + synthetic scenarios only (cross-domain association chains, temporal event chains, entity co-occurrence)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper frames prior systems' 'Uniform treatment' (S1: 'All memories receive equal importance regardless of type, age, or access patterns') as a design failure and treats false-positive retrieval of misleading memories as costlier than false negatives (S3.3.1); mitigated via asymmetric importance plasticity (additive boost eta_I=0.025 on positive feedback vs multiplicative decay delta_I=0.10 on negative feedback, Eq.2, with a recovery floor Imin=0.05) plus the piecewise decay model (aggressive early exponential clears noise within tc=3 days before transitioning to a heavy-tailed power-law, Eq.1).
cita: Sharma (2026). Shodh-Memory: A Cognitive Memory System for Edge-Native AI Agents.
notes: NOTE: the PDF's own title ('...A Cognitive Memory System for Edge-Native AI Agents') differs from the corpus input.jsonl title ('...A Neuroscience-Grounded Cognitive Memory Architecture for Artificial Intelligence Agents') -- same key/author/content, apparently a later preprint revision; on-topic, not flagged RECONSIDERAR. S3.1: three-tier Cowan-model hierarchy (T1 Working, capacity=100 items; T2 Session, RocksDB+Vamana/SPANN; T3 Long-Term, unlimited semantic-fact store) with biologically-motivated promotion thresholds (working->session: importance>=0.35 & age>=30min; session->long-term: importance>=0.5 & age>=24h) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO;EPISODICA;SEMANTICA, operaciones includes ADMISION (the promotion gate). S3.2 piecewise exponential-to-power-law decay (Eq.1, tc=3days) + Imin=0.05 floor -> OLVIDO. S3.3 dual plasticity: importance plasticity (Eq.2, asymmetric feedback-driven update) + Hebbian synaptic plasticity (Eq.3, tier-dependent learning rates) + multi-scale LTP (Burst/Weekly/Full) -> ACTUALIZACION. S3.5 Semantic Consolidation: episodic memories aged>=7days clustered by Jaccard similarity (>=2 supporting memories) converted to semantic facts via a multi-extractor pipeline, runs 'during idle periods' -> CONSOLIDACION, trigger=CHECKPOINT (idle-period consolidation)+EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (Hebbian update on co-activation). 'Compressed semantic memories retain LZ4-compressed provenance links to source episodic memories' (S3.5) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F. S3.4 retrieval fuses BM25(Tantivy)+vector(MiniLM-L6-v2)+graph spreading-activation (ACT-R-inspired, Eq.6) with density-dependent fusion weights (Eq.7) -> retrieval=RANKING;EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO, representacion=HIBRIDA. S5.1 explicit scope statement: 'comprehensive retrieval accuracy evaluation on standardized benchmarks such as LOCOMO... remains important future work'; only internal Criterion.rs latency/throughput microbenchmarks (Tables3-5, sub-20ms end-to-end) + synthetic-scenario Precision@k/Recall@k/MRR comparisons of graph-augmented vs vector-only retrieval (20-40% Recall@5 / 30% MRR gains, explicitly caveated as 'controlled scenarios, not standardized datasets') -> mide_lectura=SI (retrieval-quality metrics ARE reported, just not on a named benchmark) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F; evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (graph-vs-vector-only isolation)+MEDICION-COSTO (extensive latency/throughput/scaling tables). S4.2.1 Multi-Tenant Isolation (SLB sharded per session_id) -> alcance=SESION ('Session Memory' is the paper's own T2 tier name); multiagente=NO (isolation design, not sharing, matches F_screening's absent MULTIAGENTE tag). benchmarks: MS-MARCO, LoCoMo, ReAct agent (synthetic), Wikipedia single-pool (own)
fallos_mitigaciones: Multi-hop queries requiring evidence from semantically distant regions of memory are a genuine limitation of bucket-based routing: LoCoMo multi-hop category shows a -17% deficit vs dense retrieval (Table5, S'Discussion'); mitigated via a confidence-gated Hybrid RM-Dense Fallback (Eq.7, S3.6) that recovers 67% of the RM-dense gap at gamma=0.65 with only 13.6% of queries falling back to dense retrieval (Table6).
cita: Sertel (2026). Routing Memory: Lightweight Long-Term Memory for Agentic LLMs via Vector-Quantized Routing.
notes: S3.2-3.3: VQ codebook (K-means, K=256) assigns 1-2 byte routing codes per item -> 768x compression vs fp16 dense embeddings (Table1); multi-bucket probe (top-n centroids, Eq.2) + intra-bucket cosine reranking (Eq.3) -> representacion=VECTOR (still fundamentally embeddings, just quantized), retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING. mem_tipos=NA: RM is a content-agnostic routing/indexing LAYER demonstrated interchangeably over MS-MARCO passages, LoCoMo conversation turns, ReAct agent traces, and Wikipedia paragraphs (S4 Datasets) -- it does not define what TYPE of content is memorized, only HOW it is indexed/retrieved. operaciones=WRITE only (initial batch codebook training + item encoding); trigger=NA and no ADMISION/CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION: the codebook 'is static after training; online updates for streaming data are not currently supported' (S7 Limitations) -- no runtime write-triggering or memory-mutation policy is described, only offline/batch index construction. mide_lectura=SI: Recall@k/MRR/cluster-purity are the paper's primary and near-exclusive evaluation currency across Tables2-15 -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. S5.4/Table4-5 LoCoMo: session-aware embedding enrichment (Eq.5, prepends session/date/speaker metadata to each turn before encoding; 'queries are not enriched') surpasses Dense Recall@5 by +16.4% (0.272 vs 0.234), +81% on Temporal category, but -17% on Multi-hop -> alcance=SESION (LoCoMo's session-structured conversational memory is the flagship agent-memory demonstration), fallos_mitigaciones/NEGATIVO(b) anchor. S5.7/Table8-10 score-based passage filtering cuts LLM context tokens 37-42% same-domain / 75-78% cross-domain (Table14, million-scale); Table10 projects $318-$31,800/month savings at 1M queries across 4 commercial APIs -> COSTO in F, metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. S6 Table15 codebook-K ablation + S5.3 cluster-purity-vs-recall decomposition + S5.8.1 K-selection heuristic comparison -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. S5.10 million-scale (1M items): RM maintains ~100% recall ratio to dense at 732x compression and 2x latency advantage -> BENCHMARK-E2E. F_screening was RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO; full text confirms and adds WRITE (index construction) and NEGATIVO (multi-hop deficit, Table5).

benchmarks: NINGUNO (own long-running production-style serving workload; evaluated against TTL and LRU baselines under identical workloads; no standardized external benchmark used)
fallos_mitigaciones: TTL bounds item AGE but not COMPUTATIONAL FOOTPRINT: retrieval candidate-set and vector-scan work grow unbounded as retained items accumulate, producing heavy-tailed latency (13.8% of requests exceed 2s, S2). LRU is 'value-agnostic... can evict long-lived but high-utility information under phase shifts' (S1/S4). Both are mitigated by AMV-L's value-driven tiered eligibility (hot/warm/cold, Eq. unified value-update rule Sec.5) that decouples total retained memory from the request-path retrieval-eligible set (S4.5 system invariant), cutting the >2s-request fraction to 0.007% relative to TTL.
cita: Bamidele (2026). AMV-L: Lifecycle-Managed Agent Memory for Tail-Latency Control in Long-Running LLM Systems.
notes: S4-6: three-tier lifecycle (hot/warm/cold) with a continuously-updated scalar utility value V(m) (unified update rule S5.2: V(m) <- min{V(m)*e^(-lambda*Dt) + alpha*I_access + beta*I_contrib, Vmax}), value-driven promotion/demotion/eviction (theta_E eviction threshold applies only in cold tier) with hysteresis to prevent oscillation -> operaciones=WRITE(insertion)+ADMISION(tier-eligibility gate for the hot/warm retrieval-candidate set)+OLVIDO(cold-tier eviction)+ACTUALIZACION(continuous per-item value update, S5). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(value updated 'lazily when an item is touched by a request')+CHECKPOINT(tier migration/eviction performed asynchronously 'off the critical path' as background maintenance, S4.3). representacion=VECTOR (each item carries content/metadata/embedding/scalar-value; shared vector index with candidate-ID tier scoping, S8). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING (cosine similarity top-n over the tier-bounded candidate set R=T_H u Sample_k(T_W), S7). mem_tipos=TRABAJO (the hot tier literally IS the bounded 'request-path working set', the paper's central framing) + SEMANTICA (user facts/preferences, domain facts) + EPISODICA (summaries of prior interactions) -- S2: 'Memory records include user facts and preferences, summaries of prior interactions, intermediate task artifacts, retrieved documents, and system-generated observations'. plan_estado=SI: 'intermediate task artifacts'/'intermediate task state' are EXPLICITLY named memory content types (S1: 'autonomous services maintain intermediate task state over extended executions'; S2). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: S8 request path 'records which memory was used in the answer for attribution and feedback, and returns the answer with citations' -> explicit provenance/attribution mechanism -> FIDELIDAD in F. mide_lectura=SI: retrieval QUALITY is explicitly preserved and measured across policies -- 'matching retrieval quality (value means within ~0-2%)' vs LRU (abstract) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=PROYECTO: framing is long-running per-deployment/per-agent persistent memory beyond any single session ('coding agents retain project context... over extended executions', S1), not scoped to one conversational session. Abstract headline: vs TTL, AMV-L improves throughput 3.1x, reduces latency 4.2x(median)/4.7x(p95)/4.4x(p99), cuts >2s-request fraction 13.8%->0.007%; vs LRU trades +26%/+3% median/p95 for -15% p99/-98% >2s and ~6% fewer tokens/request at matched retrieval quality -> COSTO+LATENCIA in metricas, MEDICION-COSTO, BENCHMARK-E2E (full-stack production-style serving system evaluated under identical long-running workloads vs 2 baselines). No internal ablation of AMV-L's own components found (grep for ablat/hysteresis-disabled sensitivity study returns nothing) -> evidencia_tipo excludes ABLATION. NEGATIVO(b): TTL's and LRU's failure modes under long-running accumulation are direct negative findings about common (naive) memory-retention strategies. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text finds NO content-consolidation mechanism (pure numeric lifecycle/tiering, not memory-content merging) so CONSOLIDACION is DROPPED and replaced with WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

benchmarks: NINGUNO (no external community benchmark; own single-user corpus of 4,182 Claude-Code conversations / 14,340 exchanges across 6 SE projects + 201 curated recall queries evaluated across 107 search configurations)
fallos_mitigaciones: Prevailing LLM-compaction-under-context-pressure is 'lossy summarization... no schema, no extraction targets, no contract about what survives... summaries of summaries degrade iteratively, information from early exchanges is progressively destroyed' (S1); mitigated by structured distillation with a mandatory verbatim back-reference (ground truth is never discarded, only indexed) plus the 'surviving vocabulary principle' (LLM told to reuse exact participant terminology rather than paraphrase freely) -- only 27.0% of top-15-IDF verbatim tokens survive into distilled text, yet 96.8% of QUERY vocabulary is retained (S3.2), explaining why retrieval quality survives aggressive compression.
cita: Lewis (2026). Structured Distillation for Personalized Agent Memory: 11x Token Reduction with Retrieval Preservation.
notes: S3.2 Table1: each exchange -> compound 'palace object' (exchange_core+specific_context LLM-generated / room_assignments LLM-generated thematic tags / files_touched regex-extracted), each carrying a back-reference (conversation_id/ply_start/ply_end) to its verbatim source -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA (per-exchange conversation memory), representacion=HIBRIDA (structured text objects + separate FAISS vector index [MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim] + BM25 lexical index, S3.3), fidelidad_procedencia=SI (explicit back-reference/drill-down provenance + two-tier index-vs-display separation, 'the user always reads the unmodified original', S3.2/contribution4) -> FIDELIDAD in F. operaciones=WRITE(distillation)+ADMISION(<100-char exchanges filtered as trivial, S3.1). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (ply/exchange-boundary completion defines the segmentation unit, S3.1). Table2: 4,182 conversations/14,340 exchanges -> 12,427 distilled objects, 371->38 avg tokens = 11x corpus-level compression (9.9x per-item). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(HNSW/Exact vector)+RANKING(BM25-Okapi/BM25-FTS lexical scoring + RRF/Weighted/Additive/CombMNZ fusion, S3.4). mide_lectura=SI: the paper's ENTIRE evaluation (107 configs, 201 queries, 214,519 consensus-graded pairs, 5 local LLM graders + calibrated Opus 6th-grader, S4.3-4.4) is a direct measurement of retrieval-quality preservation under compression -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. S5.1-5.2 Table3: best pure-distilled config reaches 96% of best-verbatim MRR (0.717 vs 0.745); best cross-layer (BM25-verbatim + HNSW-distilled fusion) slightly EXCEEDS best-verbatim (MRR 0.759, 102%) -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Mechanism-dependent result: vector search (HNSW/Exact) shows NO significant degradation on distilled text (10/10 non-significant post-Bonferroni, |d|<=0.25) while ALL 20 BM25 configs degrade SIGNIFICANTLY (|d|=0.031-0.756, Table10) -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (107-config x 4-mechanism systematic comparison with significance tests), and this mechanism-dependent BM25 failure is a genuine NEGATIVO(b) finding (a naive lexical-search-over-compressed-memory combination measurably hurts recall, even though vector-search-over-compressed-memory does not). alcance=PROYECTO: single-user corpus spans 6 distinct software-engineering projects (Table2), explicitly framed as 'the intended deployment setting: persistent memory over one developer's long-running agent history' (S4.1), broader than one project yet still single-user (not multi-user/ORGANIZACION). Token-budget result (contribution3): 1,000 exchanges fit in ~39,000 tokens vs ~407,000 verbatim -> COSTO in F, metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. handoff=PUNTEROS;CONTENIDO: the distilled object is literally a pointer/index (conversation_id+ply-range) that resolves to full verbatim CONTENT when a later session recalls it -- the paper's central architectural claim (contribution4: 'two-tier architecture... separates index from display'). F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms and adds WRITE, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

benchmarks: LoCoMo & LongMemEval query taxonomies (used to derive synthetic store-routing labels, not run directly); own 150-question QA evaluation (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o-mini) + 1,000-query synthetic routing benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: S5.3 'Why Does Uniform Underperform?' identifies two failure modes of retrieving from all stores: (1) needle-in-a-haystack signal dilution at ~787 tokens, and (2) 'Conflicting information' -- LTM may retain a STALE fact that contradicts an updated Summary-store fact (worked example: LTM's pre-reorg note causes GPT-4o-mini to answer 'Michael Torres' instead of the current 'Jennifer Williams'); mitigated by selective store routing (oracle/hybrid) that avoids querying stale/irrelevant stores in the first place, cutting context tokens 62% while INCREASING QA accuracy.
cita: Gaikwad (2026). Did You Check the Right Pocket? Cost-Sensitive Store Routing for Memory-Augmented Agents.
notes: S3.1-3.2: the paper routes across 4 MemGPT-style stores -- STM (short-term/current conversation), Summary (compressed user facts/preferences/ongoing projects), LTM (summaries of past conversations), Episodic (raw transcripts) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO(STM)+SEMANTICA(Summary)+EPISODICA(LTM+Episodic). representacion=NA, retrieval=NA, operaciones=NA, trigger=NA: this paper is EXCLUSIVELY about a meta-level WHICH-STORE-to-query routing decision, explicitly bypassing within-store mechanics -- 'We concatenate full store contents instead of performing top-k retrieval within each store... production systems often apply ranking or filtering within each memory store' (S7 Limitations) -- so how content is represented/written/retrieved WITHIN a store is never defined here. mide_lectura=SI regardless: the core evaluation directly measures the downstream UTILITY of memory reading via store-selection choices (Table2: oracle 86.7% vs uniform 81.3% QA accuracy at 299 vs 787 tokens, -62% context, GPT-4o-mini) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. S5.3 'Conflicting information' example (Summary='Jennifer Williams' current manager vs LTM's stale pre-reorg 'Michael Torres' note) is a direct cross-source staleness/consistency case (FIDELIDAD 'costuras', rule7) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD in F. Table1 synthetic routing (1,000 queries/7 types): Uniform=100% coverage/8% exact-match/waste=2.9; Hybrid=94%/58%/1.2; Oracle=100%/100%/0. Table2 LLM QA (150 Qs): oracle beats uniform on BOTH accuracy (86.7% vs 81.3%) AND tokens (-62%), gap widening in the long-context regime (72% vs 60%) -> this uniform-retrieval underperformance despite MORE context is a clear NEGATIVO(b) finding -> NEGATIVO in F. S6.1 Table3 feature ablation (linguistic-only 57% coverage baseline -> +semantic signals +33pp=90% -> +embedding-similarity-tiebreak +4pp=94%) -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. S6.2: routing overhead <1ms rule-based / ~5ms embedding-based vs 500-2000ms LLM inference -> metricas=LATENCIA, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. benchmarks derive synthetic store-labels FROM LoCoMo+LongMemEval taxonomies (S5.1/S9) plus an own 150-question QA benchmark -> BENCHMARK-E2E. alcance=SESION: stores explicitly span 'current conversation' through 'historical sessions' for one user (S3.1). F_screening was COSTO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; full text confirms and adds FIDELIDAD (staleness/conflicting-source example) and NEGATIVO (uniform-retrieval-with-more-context underperforms selective routing).
